newsitem.title: USA: Snowstorm sweeps into central U.S, cold to follow.
newsitem.headline: Snowstorm sweeps into central U.S, cold to follow.

text.p: A major snowstorm hit the central U.S. Thursday, blanketing southern South Dakota, northeast Nebraska and northwest Iowa with two to five inches and accumulations could reach 10 inches in some areas by Friday, meteorologists said.

Also, frigid cold will follow the snow that could damage winter wheat this weekend from Kansas to Texas. Lows could dip to 18 degrees Fahrenheit in southwest Kansas and 25 degrees in the Texas Panhandle, forecasters said.
"We are talking about the liklihood of some damaging cold temperatures for the southern Plains wheat this weekend," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Lows were forecast to reach 18 degrees in southwest Kansas this weekend and 25 degrees in the Oklahoma Panhandle and northern Texas Panhandle, he said.

The hard red winter wheat areas will probably have the coldest weather Saturday and Sunday, while soft red winter wheat areas of the Midwest could have lows from the teens to 20 degrees Monday, said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc.
The snowstorm now in the Plains should move east, producing three to six inches in northern Illinois and southern Wisconsin, said Burgio.
"We will see snow breaking out across northern Illinois and southeast Wisconsin today and tonight, which could accumulate several inches before turning to rain," said Weather Services' Burgio.
Further south, rain amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches were foreast for the southern Midwest and Delta regions Friday and early Saturday, he said.

A short warm spell was likely next week for the central U.S., followed by more cold later in the week. However, the meteorologists said the next cold system should be milder than the one due this weekend.
Gesser said long-range forecasts suggest above-normal temperatures spreading across the central and Midwest areas April 21 and lasting up to 10 days.
He said such weather could cause a "maxmium meltdown" of snow in the northern Plains and present the greatest flood threat of the season.
